summary: This sermon examines the parable of the Good Samaritan to challenge the question 'who is my neighbor?' and reframe it as 'am I acting like a neighbor?' The preacher confronts how Christians use theology to justify limited compassion and dehumanize certain groups, while also revealing the deeper gospel layer: Jesus is the unexpected Samaritan who rescues us when we are half-dead in sin.
key_points: Stop asking who qualifies as your neighbor and start asking if you are being neighborly
Good theology is worthless without obedience and compassionate action
Christians often redefine 'neighbor' or 'love' to preserve comfort and justify inaction
The Samaritan foreshadows Jesus as the unexpected hero who sacrificially saves the dying
We are either the half-dead man needing rescue or the innkeeper entrusted to care for others
big_idea: True eternal life is found in knowing, loving, and obeying the God revealed in Jesus by extending sacrificial love to all image-bearers without redefining who counts as our neighbor.
title: PARABLES: Who is My Neighbor?
